title: Power Query: importing from files, databases and the web

videos.script: Every month the web shop sends a file. Every month somebody opens it, fixes the prices, deletes the cancelled orders, and pastes the rows under last month's. {{monthly}} It takes an afternoon. And it is never done quite the same way twice. {{afternoon}} Power Query does it differently. You open the file through it once, and you make the same fixes. Each fix becomes a step in a list. {{steps}} Next month you save the new file and press Refresh. The list runs again, in order, on the new rows. {{refresh}} This lesson is about getting data in. A text file first, and the rules that read it. A comma or a semicolon. A full stop or a comma for the decimals. The day first, or the month. {{locale}} Then a whole folder of files, read as one table. Then tables in your own workbook, and other workbooks. {{folder}} Databases and web pages get a section each. They are described, not run, because there is nothing here to connect to. {{sources}} And at the end, where the result goes. A table on a sheet, a connection, or the data model. {{load}} You will make four small files yourself, in a text editor. Lesson 14 cleans them, joins them and reshapes them. {{files}}
